- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., 60+), often overshooting by 5–15% and failing to correct downward.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; forecasts lag behind actual price movements by 3–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after high peaks, then undercorrects upward after low troughs.
- Horizon-specific: 10–15 day forecasts are most prone to underestimation; 20+ day forecasts show increasing underestimation with higher volatility.
- Avoids recent high values in history when forecasting; fails to weight recent data sufficiently, leading to underestimation of upward trends.
- Tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp price reversals or sudden spikes.
